s1.syndrome_frame: Acute abdominal pain with systemic inflammatory response
salient_findings: Positive blood cultures for gram-negative bacilli
key_facts: Consumes 400 mL of Japanese spirit daily
Ate teppanyaki with seafood 4 days prior to hospital visit
Pulse oximetry saturation: 98% at room air
Blood cultures positive for gram-negative bacilli

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute abdominal pain with systemic inflammatory response
salient_findings: Positive blood cultures for gram-negative bacilli
key_facts: Consumes 400 mL of Japanese spirit daily
Ate teppanyaki with seafood 4 days prior to hospital visit
Pulse oximetry saturation: 98% at room air

shortlist.label: Acute cholecystitis
shortlist.why_kept: Upper abdominal pain and fever, with elevated leukocyte count and C-reactive protein levels

shortlist.label: Acute pancreatitis
shortlist.why_kept: History of alcoholic acute pancreatitis and current presentation of upper abdominal pain and fever

shortlist.label: Cholangitis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated gamma-glutamyltransferase and aspartate aminotransferase levels, suggesting biliary tract involvement

shortlist.label: Gram-negative sepsis
shortlist.why_kept: Blood cultures positive for gram-negative bacilli and systemic inflammatory response

shortlist.label: Intra-abdominal abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Upper abdominal pain, fever, and elevated leukocyte count, with possibility of abscess formation

raw.rationale: The patient has a high fever, shaking chills, elevated leukocyte count with a high percentage of neutrophils, and positive blood cultures for gram-negative bacilli, which are all indicative of sepsis.

rejected.label: Acute cholecystitis
rejected.why: There is no specific evidence of gallbladder inflammation or gallstones mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Acute pancreatitis
rejected.why: Although the patient has a history of alcoholic acute pancreatitis, the current presentation and laboratory findings do not specifically suggest a new episode of pancreatitis.

rejected.label: Cholangitis
rejected.why: There is no clear evidence of biliary tract infection or obstruction, which is typically required for a diagnosis of cholangitis.

rejected.label: Intra-abdominal abscess
rejected.why: Imaging studies did not show a clear focus of infection or abscess formation in the abdomen.
